bugs: Empty optional params are rejected with 422 instead of being treated as absent (probe confirmed): ?status= gives 422 when it should default to paid, and ?from=, ?country= and ?from=2026-03-10&to= also give 422. v.rationale: The two are structurally near-twins: same invokable controller, Form Request with filters(), BuildSalesReport action, #[Scope] model scopes, Number::currency money helper, and SQL aggregation with deterministic tie-breaks. Both pass their suites (26 and 24 tests), and both produced correct totals, country breakdown, top products and top customers in my probes, including combined filters, case-insensitive country and inclusive date bounds. The deciding difference came from the probes. impl-1 uses 'nullable' rules, so empty params like ?status= or ?from=2026-03-10&to= are treated as absent and status defaults to paid. impl-2 rejects all of these with 422, which is a real usability bug for optional filters. impl-1's tests are also a bit broader: orders without items, an array status, and requests without the JSON Accept header. impl-2 is slightly cleaner in places: one joined query for top customers, a reusable $matching closure with tap(), qualified columns, and one migration per table. But it couples the migration to the app enum, cascade-deletes orders with customers, and adds a pointless no-network test. impl-1 has some ceremony of its own: a raw-SQL constant on the model, an inOrders(Builder) scope, a redundant trim, and an extra findMany. On balance, impl-1 ranks first.
